title: Canonical product identity and beta posture
description: User-facing surfaces use VaMender. Technical identifiers may use vamender, and VaM package identifiers remain AgenticCreator.VaMender. Until an approved requirement changes the channel, releases are beta and require production-grade safety evidence without claiming general availability.

title: Supported platform and host compatibility
description: Support 64-bit Windows and the verified Virt-a-Mate 1.22.0.13 runtime and install per-user without administrator rights. VaM 1.22.0.12 is expected to work based on the documented plugin impact surface but is untested. Official CI, CodeQL, release validation, packaging, and release evidence run only on GitHub-hosted Windows runners; Linux and macOS are neither supported product nor validation platforms.

title: Read-only package inventory
description: vamender check inventories the complete AddonPackages tree without modifying VARs, reports invalid archives and unresolved dependencies, and optionally CRC-reads every member when --deep is selected.

title: VaM-aware cleanup planning
description: vamender plan combines static archive evidence with a fresh VaM package-rescan log, identifies stale or absent logs, avoids describing static-only references as runtime-confirmed failures, and emits a read-only repair and dependency-closure plan.

title: Conservative metadata repair
description: Repair missing, invalid, stale, or incomplete meta.json only from package evidence or explicit user input. Never guess an unknown license or treat descriptive material, morph, or parameter labels as dependencies.

title: Proven filename and archive repair
description: Correct casing, Unicode-safe identities, supported ZIP header inconsistencies, and malformed filenames only when identity is unambiguous. Archive byte-identical malformed duplicates only after checksum comparison and whole-VAR backup.

title: Safe dependency relinking
description: Keep exact script and plugin dependencies exact. Relink a reference to a newer local version only for non-plugin content when a compatible provider exists and the relevant resource payload is proven safe.

title: Dependency-closure isolation
description: Expand failures through the installed dependency graph, distinguish a missing package from a provider missing an internal member, and isolate unusable closures without deleting scenes or substituting artistic content.

title: Conservative old-version retirement
description: Archive superseded VAR versions only after reference rewrites, dependency-closure analysis, payload compatibility, metadata-conflict checks, and post-rewrite validation all succeed.

title: Verified backup before mutation
description: Before rewriting, renaming, replacing, or archiving a VAR, copy the whole original to a durable backup root outside AddonPackages, verify SHA-256, and append a restore record to manifest.jsonl.

title: Atomic replacement and post-change validation
description: Replace a live VAR through a validated temporary artifact and an atomic or rollback-safe handoff, then recheck the archive and affected references before retiring an old version or temporary source.

title: Checksum-verified restore
description: Restore consumes VaMender manifest records, verifies backup checksums, rejects destinations outside the selected AddonPackages root, supports most-recent subsets, skips existing files by default, and preserves overwritten conflicts under restore-conflicts.

title: Predictable user reports
description: Every public operation emits actions_taken.txt, actions_required.txt, and missing_dependencies.txt. A full run retains stage evidence under _details while preserving the three top-level handoff files.

title: Explicit CLI mutation gates
description: Check and plan are read-only. Repair and migrate default to dry-run and require --apply plus a backup root to mutate. Run requires a backup root, and help states the independent-backup warning and user responsibility.

title: Constrained engine bridge
description: Bind the local bridge to installer-selected library, backup, state, and report roots; allow only supported operations; reject malformed or traversal-capable request IDs; publish state atomically; and prevent concurrent engines for one state root.

title: Sandboxed in-VaM control panel
description: The CLR 2 Session Plugin remains in VaM's sandbox, exposes supported engine operations, blocks competing requests while busy, displays lifecycle state, publishes panel and VaM-log updates only when that state changes, rescans packages after successful mutation, and never performs unrestricted AddonPackages access itself.

title: Safe per-user installation and removal
description: Setup validates VaM.exe and AddonPackages, requires a durable backup path outside AddonPackages, refuses to interrupt active or queued engine work, stops an idle tray host before replacing its executable, installs without elevation, checksum-verifies the new plugin, backs up and retires older VaMender plugin revisions, configures automatic per-user startup, and retains backups/reports on uninstall.

title: Content rights and privacy boundary
description: Never download, authenticate for, bypass access controls on, or infer licenses for paid, private, creator-restricted, or unavailable content. Local analysis does not transmit package contents or user library data.

title: Robust package compatibility
description: Handle Unicode identifiers, nested AddonPackages paths, supported ZIP compression methods, VaM-sensitive casing, and the implemented tar-compatible fallback without losing invalid-content evidence.

title: Required quality and security gates
description: Merge candidates pass pinned Specsmith synchronization/coverage/audit, Rust formatting, SPDX validation, denied-warning and cognitive-complexity Clippy, all locked Rust tests, C# compile/type-load and sandbox validation, Session Plugin VAR packaging, release build/branding/Setup validation, and CodeQL on GitHub-hosted Windows runners only. No Linux or macOS job is authoritative.

title: Reproducible GitHub Actions beta release
description: While the channel is beta, a tag uses v0.MINOR.PATCH and matches Cargo, plugin, and installer versions with a dated changelog entry. Windows-only GitHub Actions builds the executable, packages and checksums it into the portable ZIP, retains workflow artifacts, and uploads the Session Plugin VAR, Setup, and portable ZIP to a GitHub prerelease from the tagged commit. For release-only text changes, Actions verifies the approved CLR 2 DLL baseline hash and a normalized plugin-source hash before applying only equal-length version, beta URL, and Setup wording stamps. Any other plugin change is rejected until the DLL is rebuilt and validated against the supported VaM installation. Maintainer workstations are not release authorities.

title: Beta acceptance evidence
description: Beta promotion requires green automated gates plus documented supported-environment smoke evidence for install, read-only check/plan, a backed-up mutation, VaM rescan, report review, restore, and uninstall. An unexecuted environment-dependent check remains a release blocker.

title: Maintainer and user documentation
description: User and maintainer documents remain consistent with the VaMender name, beta channel, supported platform, safety model, content-rights boundary, install/restore workflow, and independent-project disclosure.
source: README.md; CHANGELOG.md; SUPPORT.md; SECURITY.md; CONTRIBUTING.md; MAINTAINERS.md; DISCLAIMER.md

title: Privacy-first support reporting
description: VaMender provides a read-only support-report command that extracts only package-related diagnostics into a local review bundle, omits absolute paths, full VaM logs, VAR payloads, manifests, credentials, and private URLs, includes a complete VAR list only by explicit opt-in, never uploads data automatically, and opens GitHub only after explicit review consent.

title: GitHub release and F95Zone announcement
description: VaMender is not submitted to VaM Hub because its moderators rejected third-party apps or scripts that modify VARs in AddonPackages. GitHub Releases is the only binary distribution channel and must contain the exact tagged Setup, Session Plugin VAR, portable ZIP, and SHA-256 sidecars. An F95Zone page may announce and discuss the release, but must link to the matching GitHub release, accurately disclose beta status, the external Windows executable, explicit mutation, verified backup, tested VaM 1.22.0.13 / expected but untested 1.22.0.12 compatibility, and project independence, and must never disguise a download as a support link. The current F95Zone rules require manual review immediately before each post.

title: Defined path to v1.0.0
description: VaMender remains beta until the documented v1.0.0 gates are met for repeated supported-environment safety evidence, restore and rollback, installer/plugin compatibility, security and signing posture, privacy-safe support, GitHub/F95Zone release disclosure, documentation, and reproducible GitHub Actions release artifacts.

title: Pseudonymous maintainer identity
description: Project-authored public commits and annotated release tags use TheAgenticCreator <312204356+TheAgenticCreatorDev@users.noreply.github.com> rather than a maintainer's legal name, personal account name, or personal email. Repository-local configuration, a pre-push guard, CI, and release gates verify the metadata. Pull-request CI validates the real head history rather than GitHub's temporary synthetic merge commit. Maintainer GitHub operations authenticate as TheAgenticCreatorDev or an approved organization App because commit metadata cannot conceal GitHub's authenticated event actor.

title: Windows tray-host lifecycle
description: The per-user Windows host presents a VaMender notification-area icon, starts the constrained engine from a dedicated GUI-subsystem host executable without a console or external script, keeps it available across ordinary VaM launches, launches VaM on request, opens report and backup folders, reports product/version and safety information, toggles Start with Windows, and exits cooperatively after any in-flight operation finishes. The same busy-aware cooperative shutdown is available to Setup before executable replacement. Setup enables Start with Windows by default, and VaM's plugin sandbox is not used to spawn or terminate the host.
